name: Dasatinib
drug_class: BCR-ABL and SRC-family tyrosine kinase inhibitor (second generation)
owner: Bristol Myers Squibb (Sprycel); generic in many markets

discovery.note: An aminothiazole carboxamide originally developed as an SRC inhibitor that also binds the active conformation of ABL.

tagline: Second-generation BCR-ABL inhibitor active against most imatinib-resistant mutants
summary: Dasatinib is a multi-targeted kinase inhibitor that binds both the active and inactive conformations of ABL and is about 300 times more potent than imatinib in vitro. It is used for Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukaemia and acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, including after imatinib resistance, although it is inactive against T315I.
mechanism: Dasatinib competes with ATP at the ABL kinase domain, binding regardless of the activation-loop conformation, which allows it to inhibit many imatinib-resistant BCR-ABL mutants (but not T315I).

It also potently inhibits SRC-family kinases (including LCK, relevant to T-cell function), KIT, PDGFRβ and ephrin receptors; SRC inhibition contributes to effects on platelets and to pleural effusions.
uses: CML (all phases) resistant or intolerant to prior therapy including imatinib
Paediatric Ph-positive CML and ALL (with chemotherapy)

history.title: Discovery published
history.detail: BMS-354825 described as a dual SRC/ABL inhibitor.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Sprycel for CML and Ph-positive ALL after imatinib.

history.title: First-line CML
history.detail: DASISION leads to approval for newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: FDA approves use in children with chronic-phase CML.

history.title: Paediatric ALL
history.detail: Approval with chemotherapy for paediatric Ph-positive ALL.

history.title: Phyrago
history.detail: FDA approves a reformulated dasatinib (Phyrago) via the 505(b)(2) pathway.

pk.bioavailability: oral (absolute value not established); reduced by acid suppression

facts: Dasatinib-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension can be at least partly reversible on stopping the drug.
